extracted.intended_audience: flash fiction writers, creative writers, and editors assessing short-short work
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluative criteria for creating and judging flash fiction and related very-short forms, including word-count conventions, story-quality dimensions, common forms, and submission outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Twitterature / six-word stories
rubrics_metrics.description: 6 words (example: Hemingway: "For sale: baby shoes, never worn.")
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extremely compressed story form where every word must carry weight; often used as an extreme exercise in economy and implication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drabble / microfiction
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A formal constraint that requires precision; the exact-word limit is part of the form's identity and discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dribble / minisaga
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even tighter than a drabble; forces intense economy and often relies on implication and strong structural turns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sudden fiction
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A short-short form that allows slightly more development than microfiction but still demands focus and compression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flash fiction (market-dependent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Up to 1,000–1,500 words depending on market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common contemporary label for short-short stories; exact acceptable length varies by publication, so consult target outlet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short short story
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Borders longer short-story territory; offers more room for development but still generally prioritizes concision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Must be a complete story, not a fragment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should contain a beginning, middle, and end (however compressed); flash must still resolve or present an intelligible, whole arc rather than only a vignette without narrative closure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word economy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eliminate filler; each word must contribute to character, image, action, or thematic resonance. Test removability of words (see Quality Tests).

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong opening
rubrics_metrics.description: Orient the reader in one sentence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The opening should quickly establish scene, voice, or conflict so the reader is grounded immediately; there is little space for gradual setup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong ending
rubrics_metrics.description: The punch lands; perfect openers + weak endings fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Endings should recontextualize what came before or deliver an emotional or cognitive payoff; a vivid, decisive close is essential in flash.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implied larger story
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggests a world beyond the page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flash should hint at a broader backstory or future consequences, giving the short piece weight and resonance through implication rather than exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single scene / moment focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Usually no subplot, single character arc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constrain scope to a single event, turn, or revelation; avoid multiple arcs or scenes that dilute the impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resonance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for emotional, thematic, or imagistic aftereffects that cause readers to dwell on the story beyond its few hundred words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title as third leg
rubrics_metrics.description: Title carries 1/3 of meaning in flash.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the title as an active element of storytelling—it should add information, misdirect, or otherwise work in concert with the prose to create meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surprise + inevitability
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strive for an ending or shift that surprises but also feels earned; the best micro-turns reframe prior detail so the outcome seems inevitable in retrospect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sound and rhythm
rubrics_metrics.description: Closer to lyric than to extended narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay attention to sentence-level music, cadence, and word choice; sonic qualities often carry more of the piece's effect in flash than extended plot mechanics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms of Flash
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms listed include: the list essay/story; the single-image story; the two-character vignette; the hermit-crab story (borrowed form: recipe, instruction manual, obituary); the braided micro; the single-sentence story; the found-object story; the catalogue story; the dictionary entry / Wikipedia parody. Choosing a form can guide structure and reader expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Famous Flash Outlets
rubrics_metrics.description: Representative markets that publish flash fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outlets noted: Brevity, SmokeLong Quarterly, NANO Fiction, Wigleaf, Flash Fiction Online, Vestal Review. Consult individual outlet guidelines for word counts and submission rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Tests (heuristics)
rubrics_metrics.description: A short checklist of reading/editing tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions to apply to a draft: Can you remove any word? Does the title contribute meaning? Does the ending recontextualize the opening? Does the reader want to re-read? Does it suggest more than it shows? Use these as iterative editing filters.
